capacityPolicy.source: Confluence SOP: Resource Planning, Jira Management and Tempo Time Logging

register.summary: OEM/brand partner agreements must be in place before product listing
register.context: Product listings require signed OEM/brand partner agreements. This dependency is jointly owned by the Product and Business teams and is currently open.
mitigation: Initiate OEM agreements in parallel with development work
Track agreement status via a procurement checklist
Block listing publication until agreement status is confirmed
register.why: 27 AI-server listings for Dell, HPE, NVIDIA, Supermicro and Lenovo were moved to production between 16 and 22 Sep. The register's own mitigation says to block publication until OEM agreements are confirmed.
register.action: Confirm OEM agreement status per brand before products are enabled.

register.summary: Scope creep from multiple managed service teams adding portal requirements
register.context: Multiple managed service teams are independently adding portal requirements, risking scope creep. Currently In Progress.
mitigation: Enforce a formal change request process for new requirements
Require product owner gate approval before requirements enter the backlog
Use a phased delivery roadmap with MoSCoW prioritisation
register.why: Scope creep is visible now: 192 USP issues created in 30 days and 72 open bugs.
register.action: Enforce the change-request gate named in the mitigation.

register.summary: Gynger API sandbox access required before financing integration
register.context: Financing integration on the Marketplace requires Gynger API sandbox access, which has not yet been granted.
mitigation: Request Gynger sandbox access as early as possible
Build a mock integration layer to unblock development while access is pending
Swap mock layer for real sandbox once access is granted
register.why: Financing modal is part of the PDP story (MT-1217, in UAT). No Jira evidence that Gynger sandbox access was obtained.
register.action: Confirm whether financing is in go-live scope. If not, close. If yes, assign an owner.

register.summary: Identity provider (Azure AD B2C) outage affecting login
register.context: An Azure AD B2C outage would prevent Marketplace login entirely if no fallback exists.
mitigation: Maintain a fallback authentication path
Monitor Azure AD B2C via its published SLA
Surface a status page / clear error messaging on login failure
register.why: Still valid for checkout go-live. Untouched and unassigned for 78 days.
register.action: Assign to Identity lead and link to USP-3751, which covers the same outage.

register.summary: Regulatory non-compliance (GDPR/CCPA) on cookie handling
register.context: Cookie handling must comply with GDPR and CCPA; non-compliance carries regulatory and reputational risk.
mitigation: Integrate a consent management platform for cookie handling
Conduct a quarterly compliance review
Document compliance status for Legal/Compliance sign-off
register.why: Marketing site shipped GDPR cookie consent (MR-760, Done). No equivalent evidence for Marketplace.
register.action: Confirm Marketplace consent coverage, then close or assign.

register.summary: Uvation Rewards Platform API required for service credit sync
register.context: Service credit sync depends on the Rewards Platform API, currently tracked as an open dependency.
mitigation: Implement idempotent async processing via Service Bus
Run an hourly reconciliation job to catch missed/duplicate syncs
Alert Backend team on reconciliation discrepancies
register.why: Depends on Rewards API. Same failure mode as MT-1099, which Marketplace has already mitigated.
register.action: Reuse the Marketplace sync and reconciliation pattern.

register.summary: Service credit sync failure from Marketplace or Rewards
register.context: Service credit sync from Marketplace or Rewards can fail, risking inconsistent balances for customers.
mitigation: Implement idempotent async processing via Service Bus
Run an hourly reconciliation job
Alert on discrepancies detected during reconciliation
register.why: Duplicate of USP-3750 in substance.
register.action: Merge with USP-3750.

register.summary: Azure AD B2C tenant config must be active before Marketplace auth works
register.context: Marketplace authentication depends on the Azure AD B2C tenant being active and correctly configured. This is currently an open dependency owned by the Identity Team.
mitigation: Coordinate early with the Identity Team on tenant configuration and timeline
Monitor Azure AD B2C SLA for the tenant
Maintain a fallback authentication path in case the tenant is unavailable
register.why: Azure AD B2C tenant is live. Marketplace login works in production and Identity is now removing token claims (ID-679 to ID-686).
register.action: Close as realised dependency.

register.summary: CDN infrastructure must be operational to serve product images
register.context: Product image delivery depends on CDN infrastructure being operational. This is owned by DevOps and currently open.
mitigation: Validate CDN uptime SLA
Implement fallback image hosting for CDN outages
Monitor CDN health as part of standard observability
register.why: Product images are served on production for all migrated products (MT-1528). CDN is operational.
register.action: Close as realised dependency.

register.summary: Payment gateway downtime at checkout
register.context: Checkout currently has no automatic failover if the primary payment gateway experiences downtime, risking lost orders.
mitigation: Implement dual payment provider failover
Process orders asynchronously via a queue so brief outages don't lose transactions
Alert the Backend team on gateway failure
register.why: Cart, PO upload and checkout stories are done (MT-1219), so payment gateway downtime is now a live exposure. Unassigned for 78 days.
register.action: Assign an owner and confirm failover approach before checkout is enabled.

register.summary: OEM pricing changes without notice impacting listed prices
register.context: OEMs can change pricing without notice, and Marketplace listings can drift out of sync, creating pricing-accuracy risk.
mitigation: Build automated price-sync jobs against OEM pricing feeds
Add "starting from" display guard logic where exact price can't be guaranteed
Alert Product team on large/unexpected price deltas
register.why: Listed AI-server prices depend on OEM pricing. Listings are now in production (disabled). Unassigned for 78 days.
register.action: Agree the price-sync or 'price on request' rule before enablement.

register.summary: Rewards platform sync failure leading to incorrect point balances
register.context: Sync failures between Marketplace and the Rewards platform can leave customers with incorrect point balances.
mitigation: Implement idempotent, event-driven sync between Marketplace and Rewards
Add a manual reconciliation process for detected discrepancies
Alert Backend team on repeated sync failures

lastComment.author: Naveen Jangid
lastComment.text: Event based sync mechanism is already implemented and manual sync of the orders are possible and rewards admin can also adjust the loyalty points balance through admin

register.why: Mitigation delivered. Event-based sync, manual order sync and admin point adjustment exist (comment 16 Sep). Ticket is Done.
register.action: Close in register.

register.summary: Data breach exposing customer PII or order history
register.context: Customer PII and order history are high-value targets; a breach would have critical impact and reputational/legal consequences.
mitigation: Enforce encryption at rest and in transit for all PII and order data
Enforce role-based access control (RBAC) across services touching this data
Maintain a SOC2 audit trail for access to sensitive data

lastComment.author: Naveen Jangid
lastComment.text: @Saravana Kumar @Naman Bapna I have made the changes to user get_userinfo API to get user details instead of the claims for marketplace fe and pushed to development

register.why: Userinfo API now used instead of token claims (7 Sep). Ticket is In Production. Claims-removal subtasks ID-679 to ID-683 are still in UAT.
register.action: Close once ID-679 to ID-683 reach production and Security signs off.

register.summary: Uvation Identity must remain single source of truth for USP auth
register.context: USP must not implement standalone authentication; all auth flows must delegate to Azure AD B2C via OAuth 2.0.
mitigation: No standalone auth implementation exists in USP
All authentication delegated to Azure AD B2C via OAuth 2.0
Periodic audit confirms no auth bypass paths exist
register.why: Owned and dated.
register.action: Run the periodic auth-bypass audit named in the mitigation.

register.summary: Cloud partner APIs (Azure Monitor / GCP) must be accessible for dashboards
register.context: Phase 3 dashboard work depends on cloud partner API access being validated ahead of build start.
mitigation: Validate partner API access against existing agreements
Confirm access before Phase 3 build kickoff
Document access/authentication method for the dashboard team
register.why: Owned and dated.
register.action: Confirm partner API access before Phase 3.

register.summary: Azure AD B2C outage preventing USP portal login
register.context: An Azure AD B2C outage would block USP portal login entirely without mitigation in place.
mitigation: Rely on Azure's 99.99% SLA as the baseline
Maintain cached session tokens so active sessions survive brief outages
Link a status page on the login error screen
register.why: Owned and dated.
register.action: Merge with MT-1096 into one cross-platform identity risk.

register.summary: Cloud partner API rate limits blocking dashboard data
register.context: Cloud partner API rate limits can block real-time dashboard data from loading.
mitigation: Implement a caching layer with a 5-minute TTL
Gracefully degrade to last-known data with a visible timestamp when rate-limited
Alert Engineering team when sustained rate-limiting is detected
register.why: Owned and dated.
register.action: Review at 30 Sep.

register.summary: AI transcription service failure after advisory session
register.context: The AI transcription service can fail after an advisory session, currently flagged as needing verification of applicability.
mitigation: Fall back to manual transcript delivery via email within a 4-hour SLA
Implement a retry queue for failed transcription jobs
Verify this failure mode's applicability with the advisory workflow owner (per register comment)
register.why: Owned and dated.
register.action: Confirm the failure mode applies to the advisory workflow.

register.summary: Low adoption of self-service portal by clients used to manual engagement
register.context: Clients accustomed to manual engagement may be slow to adopt the self-service portal, risking underuse of the platform.
mitigation: Build an in-portal guided onboarding tour
Have the Success Team run dedicated outreach to at-risk clients
Offer a demo-credit incentive to encourage first use
register.why: Owned and dated.
register.action: Review at 30 Sep.

register.summary: Vendor API approval delays blocking integrations
register.context: External vendor API approvals are on the critical path for several USP integrations and are prone to delay.
mitigation: Coordinate early with external vendors on approval requirements
Track approval status weekly
Build mock APIs to unblock parallel development while approvals are pending
register.why: Owned and dated.
register.action: Review at 30 Sep.

register.why: Parent epic for the Marketplace register. Children were never refreshed after 7 Jul.
register.action: Refresh all children in the next status review and assign one owner per child.

evidence: Suganya Murugaraj researched and validated attribute values for Dell, HPE, Supermicro and Lenovo between 15 and 22 Sep (PC-133). She has now moved on to NVIDIA Vera Rubin.
Naman Bapna created 27 AI-server listings on UAT and moved them all to production between 16 and 22 Sep (MT-1500 to MT-1512, MT-1528).
The Confluence 30/60/90 plan for the Product Research & Upload team already defines the roles this hire would fill.

issues.title: Policy change identified during UAT is not recorded anywhere in Jira
issues.impact: Not measurable from Jira. The change is not logged, so its effect on scope, dates and effort cannot be traced.
issues.rootCause: No change-request ticket type, and no UAT sign-off step that captures business-policy changes. About 300 tickets mentioning policy or change requests across 8 projects were checked. The closest are the returns-policy use cases (MT-1116, MT-1180, MT-1181, MT-1187) and MT-1286, which made the return-eligibility window configurable on 2 Sep. None of them records a change found in UAT.
issues.preventive: Log it now as a Change Request with impact and effort, linked to the affected stories. Add a 'business rules confirmed' line to UAT sign-off covering returns, refunds, loyalty points and pricing. Open business-rule questions already exist on MT-978 (loyalty points) and MT-1488 (refund and exchange timelines).

issues.title: Marketplace scope changed mid-sprint to AI servers only
issues.impact: A 38-task category-disable plan was added on 10 Sep. 36 are done and about 43 hours were logged against it. The home page is being redesigned around B300, GB300 and Vera Rubin (MT-1524, due 30 Sep).
issues.actionTaken: Category disable executed in 12 days. URL disposition (MT-1447) and performance check (MT-1475) remain open.
issues.preventive: Route strategy changes through a change request with an impact estimate before tasks are raised.

utilisationNotes.attributionWarning: Tempo writes every worklog to Jira under its own app account, so Jira cannot say who logged an hour. Hours here are credited to each ticket's current assignee. When a developer's ticket is handed to QA, the developer's hours move with it. Any day above 10 hours for one person is flagged for this reason.
utilisationNotes.overheadGap: Meetings, stand-ups and leave are logged against 13 shared overhead tickets in Uvation Projects. Jira returns only the oldest 20 worklogs per ticket, so recent overhead time is invisible here.

deepDives.finding: Logged 28 hours on 6 days, all on PC-133. That averages 4.7 hours a day against an 8-hour day. No hours appear in Jira for 9, 10 and 11 Sep, and 15 Sep shows 1.5 hours.
deepDives.context: The 5.5 hours on 17 Sep covered Dell GPU corrections with Naman and then HPE validation, which is 3 products. Each product also needed a tech-spec table, long description, short description and product-card copy in HTML. Across the window she validated 19 products for 4 brands, about 1.5 hours per product.
deepDives.question: Where are the other 3 or so hours a day? They may be on overhead tickets, which Jira hides, or unlogged.
deepDives.verify: Pull Suganya's Tempo timesheet for 9–22 Sep and compare the total with 72 hours.

deepDives.finding: Jira credits Sapavat with 120.8 hours, including 23.2 hours on 9 Sep. That is impossible for one person and shows developer time on tickets reassigned to QA.
deepDives.context: Sapavat's own QA tasks show 0.5 to 2 hours each. For example, the navigation, homepage-module and facet UI updates for the category disable took 1 hour each (MT-1455 to MT-1457). Functional test on staging took 1.5 hours and the toggle test 1.5 hours (MT-1471, MT-1473).
deepDives.question: Sapavat's real hours cannot be separated from developer hours in Jira. The Tempo worker report is the only reliable source.
deepDives.verify: Pull Sapavat's Tempo timesheet by worker. Check that QA time is logged on QA subtasks, not on development subtasks.
